title: When the Oath Wakes
premise: Paloma Zhou has spent her life guarding the Hollow Gate, the last sealed passage between the human realm of Thornfell and the fading fae dominion beyond, believing the covenant that closed it was mercy. When a century-old prophecy names tonight's date as the night the gate wakes, she discovers the oath was never broken by the fae — it was broken by her own ancestors, who stole the winter-heart that keeps both realms alive. Hunted by smugglers, zealot wardens, and a fae exile who claims to be her kin, Paloma must carry the winter-heart through the mountains and reforge the covenant at the gate's origin-stone before the long winter buries Thornfell forever. She succeeds only by surrendering her keeper's post and becoming the living hinge between realms — an oath renewed not in stone, but in herself.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former mountain-rescue dispatcher who grew up on border-town folklore and never quite stopped believing the fog was listening. They write fantasy about people who keep things — gates, secrets, promises — and what it costs when those things start keeping them back.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma makes her nightly rounds of the Hollow Gate, cataloguing smuggler trails and sealing hairline cracks, while her mentor Bram warns her to stop reading the restricted prophecy folio. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet competence shadowed by restlessness — she guards a door she has never been allowed to question.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Paloma finds tonight's exact date inked in the century-old prophecy book, describing 'the keeper who opens.' Before she can decide whether it's forgery or fate, the gate shudders and a wounded fae exile, Sef, collapses on her threshold pursued by warden hunters. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: vertigo — her ordered world cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Warden-Captain Ilsa Vane arrives to arrest Sef and confiscate the prophecy, revealing the Order has known of the date for years and plans to seal the gate permanently — with Paloma inside if necessary. Paloma hides Sef in the smuggler tunnels she alone knows. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: first betrayal; loyalty to the Order begins to fracture.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Fleeing through Thornfell's hidden passes, Sef tells Paloma the truth: the covenant broke when her ancestors stole the winter-heart from the fae realm, and the long winter falling now is the debt coming due. POV: alternating Paloma/Sef. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; each recognizes the other's loneliness.

chapters.title: Bram's Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts Bram, who admits he helped hide the theft a generation ago and begs her to let the old lie stand for peace's sake. She refuses; he gives her his keyring anyway. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief — love and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: In the lowland town of Corrow, Paloma trades a smuggler's secret for supplies and is recognized by Vane's informants; a childhood friend sells her out for a pardon. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as transactional — she has never truly belonged anywhere.

chapters.title: Winter-Heart
chapters.summary: Sef shows Paloma the dying fae side of the pass: frost-bound villages, a court frozen mid-sentence. The winter-heart, he says, still exists — held in the Order's deepest vault beneath the gate itself. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: horror and pity; the enemy becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath
chapters.summary: Using Bram's keys, Paloma descends into the vault and finds the winter-heart — and murals proving her grandmother led the theft. Vane catches them, but hesitates when she sees the murals too. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound; power built on theft.

chapters.title: Vane's Oath
chapters.summary: Vane reveals her own secret: the Order's founders wrote the permanent-sealing order knowing it would kill the fae realm, and she has obeyed it all her life. She lets them go — then sounds the alarm anyway, bound by her own oath. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: tragic duty; loyalty as a cage.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Shattered Pass
chapters.summary: Avalanche and warden crossbows drive Paloma and Sef onto the forbidden ridge road, where the boundary between realms is thin enough to hear voices of the dead. Paloma hears her grandmother among them, unrepentant. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Court That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: They reach the frozen fae court, where Sef's kin cannot remember why they fought the humans — only that they were wronged. The Queen, half-thawed, mistakes Paloma for her stolen daughter. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: sorrow of a people erased by someone else's crime.

chapters.title: Kinship Claimed
chapters.summary: Sef confesses the prophecy's darker line: the covenant can be reforged only by blood of both realms, and he believes Paloma is his cousin — her grandmother took more than the heart. Paloma rejects him and storms off alone. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: identity shaken; belonging offered as a claim, not a gift.

chapters.title: Alone on the Long Winter Road
chapters.summary: Paloma travels solo toward the gate, surviving a whiteout by the smuggler lore she once disdained, and realizes every skill she owns came from the borderlands' outcasts — her true community. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: self-reliance hardening into self-knowledge.

chapters.title: The Zealots of the Sealed Door
chapters.summary: She is captured by a warden splinter sect that worships the sealed gate as holy and intends to sacrifice 'the keeper who opens' at the origin-stone. Among them is her sold-out friend from Corrow, now a convert. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: captivity; faith weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Sef Returns
chapters.summary: Sef infiltrates the sect's camp to free her, nearly dying; Paloma saves him instead, accepting the kinship she refused. They escape together as the sect burns its own camp behind them. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: trust reforged under fire.

chapters.title: The Origin-Stone
chapters.summary: At the stone where the covenant was first sworn, they find the ritual requires the winter-heart returned willingly by a descendant of the thieves — and guarded there by Vane, who has chosen to make her stand. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: convergence; all debts come due in one place.

chapters.title: Three Oaths, One Stone
chapters.summary: Vane fights not to stop them but to test whether their conviction outweighs her order; defeated, she kneels and adds her warden's oath to the rite, breaking her Order rather than the world. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: redemption through chosen disobedience.

chapters.title: The Gate Wakes
chapters.summary: The rite begins, but the winter-heart demands a price: a keeper must bind herself to the gate forever, feeling every crossing, every breach, every cold. Paloma steps forward before Sef or Vane can volunteer. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely chosen, not demanded.

chapters.title: Climax: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: As the sect, the Order, and the thawing fae host converge on the stone, Paloma speaks the new covenant — truth for truth, winter shared instead of stolen — and drives the winter-heart into the gate. Light splits the storm; the long winter breaks. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: climax — the oath answered by all three realms at once.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: The gate stands open but governed: Paloma, now its living hinge, mediates the first honest crossing in a century while Vane reforms the wardens and Sef carries word home. Bram arrives to apologize; she lets him stay as her clerk. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: weary, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Opens
chapters.summary: Paloma rewrites the prophecy folio in her own hand, striking the old lies and adding the true cost of the covenant, so no future keeper inherits a beautiful falsehood. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: closure — truth enshrined where deception once lived.

chapters.title: First Crossing of Spring
chapters.summary: On the first thaw morning, fae and human travelers pass through the gate side by side, and Paloma feels each crossing as warmth instead of pain — the oath, remade, keeping her instead of caging her. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: belonging finally real; the door opens both ways.
